analysis.title: National Vision Holdings (EYE) 3Q26 recap: Traffic weighs on comp but profitability improves; Store openings to accelerate in FY27
key_insights: EYE rose 2.7% after the 3Q26 print vs -0.4% for the S&P 500. GS attributes the reaction to plans to accelerate FY27 store openings and improving profitability from cost-saving initiatives, despite continued traffic pressure.
3Q26 comp sales were +2.8%, a miss vs GS consensus of +3.8% and FactSet consensus of +3.4%. Average ticket rose 8.9% and customer traffic fell 5.6%.

The traffic decline was concentrated in transactions below the average ticket amount, including the entry-level bundle offer. Management said the bottom 25% of transactions by ticket value are only high-single-digit % of total sales and an even lower share of gross profit.
Management frames the traffic weakness as a deferral issue rather than a market share loss. Repeat-customer purchase cycles lengthened by about 3 weeks in the quarter vs about 2 weeks in 2Q.
The top 25% of transactions and the managed care customer cohort saw positive traffic and ticket growth.

FY26 SSS guidance was lowered to +2% to +3% from +3% to +5%, reflecting a sequential deceleration in October and continued traffic pressure in lower value transactions. GS now models SSS of +0.5% for 4Q26 and +2.5% for FY26.

Operating margin expanded 320bps in 3Q despite gross margin pressure from a mix shift toward premium products. SG&A leverage of 250bps came from store labor model efficiencies, lower variable incentive compensation and cost optimization.

FY26 adjusted operating income guidance was narrowed to $119mn-$131mn from $119mn-$139mn. At the midpoint this is 110bps of expansion excluding the 53rd week in FY25, within the long-term algorithm of 50-150bps a year.

National Vision opened 8 new stores in 3Q, all under America's Best, and narrowed FY26 openings to about 30 (excluding military locations). New FY26 stores are achieving a materially higher average ticket than prior-year openings.

FY27 store opening target introduced at 50-55 stores, about 75% unit growth y/y at the midpoint vs the 30 openings in FY26. Management cited a positive reception to the new Alpharetta, GA flagship format.

GS stays Neutral and raises the 12-month price target to $24 from $23 on estimate changes. Price is $18.57, 29.2% upside to target. GS stays on the sidelines because of accelerating traffic declines and competitive concerns as EYE leans into higher income, managed care customers.

GS cut FY26E adjusted EBITDA to $224.4mn from $230.9mn. FY27E/FY28E adjusted EBITDA is $253.2mn/$280.7mn (from $253.9mn/$285.3mn). A new FY29E of $318.7mn was introduced. 4Q26E sales were cut 10.4% to $475.0mn and 4Q26E adjusted EPS goes to $0.00 from $0.16.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised to $24 from $23 on estimate changes. GS stays on the sidelines because of accelerating traffic declines and competitive concerns as the company targets higher income, managed care customers.

sector_views.rationale: Value-seeking, lower-income and cash pay customers are deferring purchases, while higher-ticket and managed care cohorts are growing.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported (EYE, 11/12): comp sales +2.8% vs GS consensus +3.8% and FactSet consensus +3.4% (miss). Ticket +8.9%, traffic -5.6%.
3Q26 reported: operating margin expanded 320bps, with 250bps of SG&A leverage.
FY26 guidance (company): SSS lowered to +2% to +3% from +3% to +5%. Adjusted operating income narrowed to $119mn-$131mn from $119mn-$139mn.
FY27 guidance (company): 50-55 new store openings vs about 30 in FY26 (excluding military locations).

GS estimates: FY26E adjusted EBITDA $224.4mn (old $230.9mn), FY26E adjusted EPS $1.01 (old $1.02), 4Q26E adjusted EPS $0.00 (old $0.16), FY27E adjusted EPS $1.17 (unchanged), FY28E adjusted EPS $1.37 (old $1.42). These are GS forecasts, not reported figures.
risk_factors: Downside: slower top-line recovery as lower-income and uninsured customers defer demand or exit the market, less trade down, exam capacity headwinds, wage-driven margin pressure, increased competition and persistently elevated costs.
Upside: better-than-expected eye care and eyeglasses demand, faster margin recovery, and a multiple re-rating if sentiment improves on better top-line results and a clear path to margin recovery.
Competitive risk as National Vision leans into higher income, managed care customers.

tension_points.bull_case: Operating margin expanded 320bps on SG&A leverage, FY26 profit guidance was narrowed, and FY27 openings are set to accelerate to 50-55 after new stores showed higher average tickets. Management views the traffic decline as purchase deferral, with the top 25% of transactions and managed care customers growing.
tension_points.bear_case: Comp missed consensus, traffic fell 5.6%, FY26 SSS guidance was cut, October decelerated further, and competition is a concern as EYE shifts toward higher income, managed care customers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slower-than-expected top line recovery as lower-income and uninsured customers defer demand or exit the market, or margins failing to recover as expected.

theme_stances.key_argument: Traffic declines are accelerating and competition is a concern as the company leans into higher income, managed care customers.
theme_stances.evidence: we remain on the sidelines based on accelerating traffic declines
